title: Unit 1A: Entertainment
subtitle: Outcomes B2, 3rd edition · Unit 1A · Workbook practice

blocks.title: 1 Read the answers to the question Do you ... much? What are the people talking about? Match the answers (1-6) to the questions (a-f).
dialogue: 1 Hardly ever nowadays. We used to get away about twice a year, but it is just too expensive now. We have got a tent, so we go camping along the local coast whenever we can.
2 Not as much as I used to. To be honest, I got really overdrawn at one point, so I had to stop. Now I pick up a bargain in the sales, but only if I really need it.
3 Not if I can avoid it. The local service is never on time and it is always packed. I tend to cycle everywhere, but I take the tube if it is pouring down.
4 All the time. I think they are a brilliant local resource. Most of them are free and you can learn such a lot. Even my kids enjoy the interactive exhibitions.
5 Whenever I get the chance. My sister lives abroad, so we use the internet a lot for email and stuff. But I also like to chat, so I end up with a huge phone bill.
6 Not as much as I would like to. I really enjoy having a day off from cooking, but it works out quite pricey. As a rule, it is usually to celebrate someone’s birthday.

items.prompt: go camping near home
items.exampleAnswer: 1 - the speaker says they go camping along the local coast.

items.prompt: use public transport
visit museums and galleries
go out to dinner
keep in touch with family and friends
travel abroad

blocks.title: 2 One word is missing in each sentence. Type only the missing word.
blocks.instructions: Do not rewrite the whole sentence. Write the one word that completes the sentence correctly.

items.prompt: I do not go to concerts much as I used to.
items.exampleAnswer: as - I do not go to concerts as much as I used to.

items.prompt: As a rule, I go out once a week, usually on Saturday evenings.
I do not read for pleasure as much as I like to.
I tend see my family just on birthdays and at Christmas.
We used go to the cinema about once a week before they put the prices up.
I check the BBC website all time. I rarely use any other sites.
She must be really busy. She ever comes to the badminton club any more.
I enjoy going to the theatre, but we only go once a while.
We used to go walking every weekend. We get up early and be out on the hills to see the sunrise.

blocks.title: 3 Choose the correct words.
blocks.instructions: Read the whole sentence, then choose the adjective that best fits the meaning.

items.prompt: The song stays in your head all day. It is very catchy / dreadful.
I could listen to it all day. The music is so inspiring, just so uplifting / weird.
I saw it twice. The plot was really exciting, just really gripping / disturbing.
Why is this play so popular? I thought it was terrible, absolutely catchy / awful.
I cannot stand her acting. She is just too much, always so dull / over-the-top.
It all sounds the same to me. It is only produced to make money, just very hilarious / commercial.

blocks.title: 4 Complete the sentences using the adjectives that were not answers in Exercise 3.
blocks.dependencyReadyText: Use the remaining words from Exercise 3. Type one adjective in each gap:

items.prompt: If the remaining word is awful: The film was absolutely ...
I could not stop laughing. The show was so funny, absolutely ...
The second half was so boring, just very ...
I would not take your kids to see it. The special effects are quite upsetting, really quite ...
I did not get it at all. The dialogue was really strange, just really ...
I cannot stop singing it. It is so easy to remember, really quite ...

blocks.title: 5 Complete B’s polite disagreement with a softening word.
blocks.instructions: Choose the missing word in each gap. Use a bit, really or that to make the disagreement sound more polite.

items.prompt: A: I love horror films. B: I am not ... keen on them, to be honest.
items.exampleAnswer: that - I am not that keen on them, to be honest.

items.prompt: A: I am really into heavy metal. B: Oh, right. I find it loud and ... scary, to be honest.
A: Was that a brilliant film? B: Did you think so? It did not ... do anything for me, I am afraid.
A: Do you listen to jazz much? B: Er, I am not ... keen on jazz. I prefer something lighter.
A: Do you fancy coming to see a musical tonight? B: Thanks, but I prefer something ... more serious.
A: Have you read the latest Philip Roth novel? B: To be honest, I am not ... interested in fiction.
A: I have seen all the Bond movies at least twice. B: Really? I am not ... fond of action movies.
